content.title: Freestyle skiing star Alex Hall: “I always try to think outside the box and stay true to myself” at Winter
content.text: In an exclusive interview with Olympics.com, the US star explains why finishing second at Milano Cortina 2026 was arguably a greater achievement than winning Olympic gold in Beijing.Picture by David Ramos/Getty ImagesAlex Hall may not have defended his slopestyle Olympic title at the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics, but the freeskier still left Italy satisfied. In an era increasingly defined by ‘spin to win’, where ever-greater rotations often outweigh originality in the eyes of judges, the USA star has consistently bucked that trend. He sees the sport as a form of expression and opts for style over scores. In Livigno, Hall stayed true to that philosophy in the slopestyle final. Unique rail techniques and a rare bring-back move on the knuckle section helped him post a Run 2 score of 85.75. It put him in provisional second, just 0.53 points behind Birk Ruud of Norway. “In terms of my skiing, I feel like that's how I stand out. I always try something different, and I always try to think outside the box. I stayed true to myself and I didn’t follow the trend,” Hall told Olympics.com. "It's obviously hard in a judged sport where there's a set of criteria and you do have to cater to them a little bit. But you try to always lean as much as you can towards what you want to do, and despite the really, really tough rail course, I did that and I'm so proud of that run. “I've been fortunate enough to get rewarded for that in the past, with my gold medal run in Beijing (2022 and again in Italy, where there were a lot of elements in my run that were pretty untraditional." True to form, the Alaska-born skier threw all caution aside for his third and final attempt, attempting the hardest run he could in his repertoire. A fall ended his bid for gold, but it hardly dampened his satisfaction as he added Olympic silver to his resume. “That's what I love so much about free skiing. You can try whatever you want and really express yourself, and I wouldn't have it any other way.” Alex Hall exclusive: “Freestyle skiing is art because there's so much self-expression” Alex Hall wins slopestyle silver for Team USA at Winter Olympics 2026 Men's Freeski Slopestyle Final - Freestyle Skiing | Milano Cortina 2026ExclusiveReplayMedal EventMen's Freeski Slopestyle Final - Freestyle Skiing | Milano Cortina 2026Watch the Men's Freeski Slopestyle Final from the Milano Cortina 2026 Olympic Winter Games, held at Livigno Snow Park on 10/02/2026, where Birk Ruud (NOR) claimed the gold medal with a winning score of 86.28, while Alex Hall (USA) secured the silver, and Luca Harrington (NZL) earned the bronzeThe stakes were high for Hall in Livigno. In addition to winning medals, he wanted to put on a show as he returned to his roots. The freeski prodigy is a dual US-Italian citizen, with his mother hailing from nearby Bologna. He also spent his formative years in Switzerland, shredding the Alps across the border. “My mum’s whole family still lives in Bologna, and a few of them came up for the qualifiers. I actually went to Livigno quite a bit when I was a kid, and skied in the spring, so it felt pretty familiar,” he continued. “A bunch of my friends from Zurich also came out to watch, so it's been sweet having a home feel to it compared to Korea and Beijing in the past two Games.”Why Alex Hall feels this silver may trump his Beijing 2022 gold in difficulty Given these internal and external pressures, Hall’s slopestyle silver from Milano Cortina 2026 was a testament to his mental strength as much as his physical ability. It was the latest addition to an already glittering CV that includes gold and silver Olympic medals, seven X Games titles, Crystal Globes in both slopestyle and Big Air and several world’s first tricks. But the 27-year-old isn’t one to drink his own Kool-Aid, and despite his unquestionable popularity in the sport, he remains humble. "Honestly, just getting any medal in slopestyle is definitely really nice. I feel like it's my speciality, and I feel it's what I truly enjoy about freestyle skiing.”Alex Hall: Freestyle skiing is more of an art formAlex Hall: Freestyle skiing is more of an art formTeam USA’s Alex Hall tells Olympics.com where his creativity comes from, and how filming helped him land slopestyle gold at Beijing 2022.Several freeskiers noted that the Milano Cortina 2026 slopestyle course was one of the most difficult they had competed on. This fact, combined with the sport's significant progression over the past Olympic cycle, made Hall consider that this silver may have been harder-earned than his gold in Beijing. "The progression's been honestly crazy the last four years, both on the jumps and the rails. That's definitely one of the best runs I've ever put down. Maybe not quite the cleanest, but in terms of technicality, it was right up there," he shared. “Part of you wants to try and defend the medal, but another part of you also knows that no one can take the gold medal you have away from you. So I didn't feel too nervous. "But I could guarantee you the run I did four years ago in Beijing would not have podiumed in Italy. So it was cool to know that I've also been upping my game the last four years and keeping up with the curve and keeping up with all the young guys coming up. “Everyone's just learned so many new tricks that it's hard to keep up, but it makes it a fun challenge and I’m beyond happy with this silver.”Add to your favourites Sign-up for free and you will be able to receive Olympic news tailored to your interests.
